response.title: what solar generator should i buy if i live in an apartment with a balcony
response.answer:
For an apartment with a balcony, I'd recommend a portable power station with a 100–200W solar panel, rather than a large solar generator designed for camping or whole-home backup.

The biggest consideration is how much direct sunlight your balcony gets. Even an expensive solar generator won't help much if your balcony is shaded most of the day.

What I'd look for

Battery: 500–1,000Wh for everyday use and emergency backup.

Solar panel: 100–200W, preferably foldable or compact enough to fit your balcony.

Battery chemistry: LiFePO₄ (LFP), for long cycle life.

Noise: Fan-cooled but relatively quiet, especially indoors.

Portability: Easy to move inside when it rains or when you're not using it.

One important distinction: the solar panel collects electricity, while the power station stores it. You can use the power station indoors and place only the solar panel on your balcony.

A convenient all-in-one choice if you want a battery and solar panel without shopping for them separately.

A compact option for laptops, internet equipment and lights. Solar panel sold separately.

2. What is your main goal?

3. What's your total budget, including panels?

One last thing: saving money on electricity and having emergency backup power are very different goals. If you're primarily trying to reduce your electric bill, a battery-based solar generator may not pay for itself quickly. Also, keep the battery indoors, secure the panel against wind, check balcony rules, and never plug a portable power station into a wall outlet to feed your apartment's wiring.
